text: Setting clear project goals is essential for success. A useful approach is to use SMART goals, which means they are Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, and Time-bound. For example, instead of saying “improve the website,” a SMART goal would be “increase mobile page speed by 20% within three months.” Breaking the project into smaller milestones helps the team track progress and stay motivated, while clearly defined deliverables—like a final report or a new feature—ensure everyone knows what to produce. Finally, stakeholder alignment is crucial. Regularly confirming that all partners agree on the priorities and expected outcomes prevents confusion and keeps the project moving in the right direction.
